newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria urges UK not to hurt "special relationship".
newsitem.headline: Nigeria urges UK not to hurt "special relationship".

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Thursday urged Britain's new Labour government not to damage the "special relationship" between the countries.

"Britain has nothing to gain by waging a diplomatic war on the federal government of Nigeria," government chief secretary Gidado Idris, the most senior civilian in the country's military administration, told British high commissioner (ambassador) to Nigeria, Graham Burton.
The comments were contained in an official statement on their meeting in the capital Abuja. The ambassador took up his position this week.
Nigeria's opposition has urged the Labour government to take a firmer stand against General Sani Abacha's government on democracy and human rights.

"I believe the world should keep up strong economic pressure and must be prepared to apply sanctions until Nigeria returns to the democratic fold," Foreign Secretary Robin Cook told his first new conference in Lond
Gidado said the comment by Cook "is capable of hurting the special relationship between Britain and Nigeria."
The West imposed sanctions on Nigeria for annulling a 1993 poll meant to restore democracy and later hanging nine minority rights activists including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa.
But opposition activists consider the sanctions token and have always blamed former colonial power Britain for not leading its Western partners to take a tougher line.

Later this year heads of government from the Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies are to review Nigeria's suspension from the organisation following Saro-Wiwa's execution and discuss whether further measures are needed.
